report.answer_text:
On September 17, 2025, the Federal Reserve cut its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points, lowering the federal funds target range from 4.25%–4.50% to 4.00%–4.25%. (federalreserve.gov)
The main reason was a weakening labor market: hiring had slowed, unemployment had edged up (though it remained low), and economic growth had moderated in the first half of the year. Inflation was still above the Fed’s 2% goal, but officials judged that the risk of further weakening in employment had grown enough to warrant a cut. (federalreserve.gov)
